correctness.rationale: For algebraically closed k of characteristic zero and the filtration cutoff 2m+1, the quotient by (x) is k[y], so every square-zero element lies in (x). The faithful Jordan-plane matrix coordinates give all and only matrices (Wa,W²b;c,Wd), with c of degree at most m and a,b,d of degree at most m−1. In the two entries involving right multiplication by W, PBW commutation replaces U by U+W, an invertible filtered change, so the stated entry spaces are attained. The c-only family supplies the affine lower bound D_m. The Ore normal form over k[T] makes the finite homogeneous coefficient equations polynomial in T, hence the projective family is proper. Scaling U identifies all nonzero fibers, so Stacks Tag 0D4I bounds their dimension by the fiber at zero without a flatness assumption. In the commutative domain, c=0 forces a=d=0, and c≠0 forces d=−a and a²=−bc. For a≠0, after removing gcd(b,c), the residual factors are coprime squares up to units, giving a=HFG, b=−HF², c=HG². With degrees r,s,t the bound r+s+t≤m−1 and the free one-dimensional simultaneous rescaling give image dimension at most D_r+D_s+D_t−1≤D_{m−1}+1≤D_m. The b-only and c-only pieces and finite union preserve that bound. Removing zero and projectivizing drops one dimension; at m=0 the projective locus is one point. This verifies the full locus including mixed parity, not a truncated quotient or a finite-field extrapolation. The finite uploaded checker was inspected, not executed, and is not needed for the proof.
residual_risks: No assertion about positive characteristic, component counts or nonreduced scheme structure.
